final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced UBS-Credit Suisse merger to be announced Sunday evening before Asian markets open, structured with massive SNB liquidity (CHF 100bn+), a federal loss guarantee (CHF 9-12bn), a token share price (CHF 0.50-1.00), and regulatory waivers under emergency powers.
minority_objections: UBS may refuse without impossible guarantees, holding all negotiating leverage
AT1 bondholders will immediately seek injunctions if written down while equity retains any value
key_conflicts: FINMA wants strict loss allocation (wipe shareholders and AT1) vs Federal Council fears voter backlash and litigation
SNB resists taking credit risk vs Federal Council wanting technocrats to absorb political heat
UBS demands maximum protection vs government must avoid appearance of blank check to voters
AT1 bondholders' contractual seniority to equity vs FINMA's potential write-down authority
key_concessions: FINMA will accept some equity value preservation if necessary to close deal by Sunday
SNB will provide CHF 100-150bn liquidity facility despite preference for private solution
Federal Council will provide CHF 9-12bn loss guarantee despite political cost
UBS will acquire only with negligible price, massive government support, and legal immunity
Credit Suisse management/board will accept total capitulation and immediate resignations
red_lines: Any solution must be announced before Asian markets open Monday morning (0100 CET)
UBS will only proceed with massive government guarantees, negligible price, and legal immunity
Cross-border regulators (Fed, BoE, MAS) must not obstruct or ring-fence local subsidiaries
AT1 write-down while preserving equity value risks immediate injunctions that could freeze the transaction
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Wealth client defection to competitors treated as secondary (10-15% attrition acceptable) despite being potential accelerant
UBS integration capacity dismissed as 'not a weekend problem' despite operational complexity
Political backlash characterized as manageable through narrative framing rather than structural constraint
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS board actually approves on Sunday morning (described as highest-risk decision point with no Plan B)
Actual weekend client/counterparty outflows reaching CHF 30-40bn threshold
AT1 bondholder litigation success in obtaining injunctions Monday morning
Cross-border regulator cooperation materializing as assumed
Market reaction Monday even with announcement (10-20% wealth client departure over 6 months assumed)
uncertainty_notes: The AT1 treatment remains the most dangerous unresolved variable with two incompatible options: Option A (convert AT1 to UBS equity, wipe CS equity) has lower legal risk but harder politics; Option B (write down AT1, preserve token equity value) enables faster execution but invites immediate litigation that could freeze the deal. The room recommends Option A but has not locked this decision. UBS board approval Sunday morning is characterized as the single highest-risk gate with no viable alternative if rejected.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Opening rationale states 'Standalone stabilization has failed: The SNB/FINMA statement on Wednesday provided liquidity backstop but did not stop the hemorrhaging' — this drove the entire shift from liquidity to merger path
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: The entire dominant solution is 'FORCED MERGER WITH UBS' with concrete structure, price (CHF 0.50-1.00/share), and timeline through Sunday announcement — this is the decision
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal loss guarantee (CHF 9-12bn) and SNB liquidity facility (CHF 100bn+) are binding components of the merger structure and UBS's conditions for proceeding — shaped the deal terms
marker_evidence.client_flight: Decisive Risk D2 states if outflows reach CHF 30-40bn by Monday 'even a merger announcement may not stop the spiral' — drove the decision for SNB to open unlimited liquidity window immediately Friday night
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Decisive Risk D4 and entire AT1 section: 'This is the most dangerous legal tripwire' with two options analyzed and Option A recommended to avoid transaction freeze — directly shaped proposed capital structure
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: The AT1 vs equity hierarchy conflict is called 'the most legally dangerous variable' and drives the recommendation for Option A (convert AT1, wipe equity) over Option B to avoid inverting seniority — determined loss allocation
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 bondholder injunctions identified as risk that 'could freeze the entire transaction' Monday morning, driving the recommendation to avoid full AT1 wipeout with equity preservation — constrained the structure
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Time constraint described as 'absolute' with detailed hour-by-hour timeline Friday 2200 through Sunday 2200, and 'Must be before Asian markets open' as a red line — drove the entire 48-hour negotiation structure
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: The announcement deadline 'No later than 2200 CET Sunday' is set because 'Must be before Asian markets open (Tokyo 0900 Monday = 0100 CET Monday)' — this timing constraint structured the entire decision sequence
